source_title: Beyond Meat, Inc. - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year 2023) with FY2024 results context
publisher_issuer: Beyond Meat, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001655210; corroborated by company earnings releases and named journalism)
company_context: Beyond Meat is a plant-based meat manufacturer whose revenue peaked in 2021 and then declined while losses, negative gross margins, and a heavy convertible-note debt load created a cash crisis. Despite a still-meaningful revenue base, the company faced structural unprofitability and a looming 2027 debt maturity, forcing a major 2025 debt restructuring.
macro_context: Post-2021 collapse in plant-based meat demand, intensifying competition and consumer price sensitivity amid inflation; tight capital markets for unprofitable consumer-growth names raised refinancing risk on its convertible debt.
outcome_category: 7 - high revenue but cash flow crisis
evidence_summary: Beyond Meat's net revenues fell from a peak of $464.7 million in 2021 to $343.4 million in 2023 and $326.5 million in 2024, while losses remained large: a net loss of $338.1 million in 2023 and $160.3 million in 2024. Gross margin turned deeply negative in Q4 2023 (gross loss of $83.9 million, or -113.8% margin) before returning to a positive $41.7 million gross profit in 2024 with still-negative operating income. The company carried roughly $1.2 billion of debt against about $131.1 million of cash (as of September 27, 2025), with a >$1.1 billion 2027 maturity it could not pay, prompting a late-September 2025 restructuring to exchange over $800 million of convertible notes for new higher-interest bonds plus large share issuance to extend maturities to 2030.
owner_decision_context: With declining revenue, negative-to-thin margins, persistent cash burn, and a >$1.1 billion 2027 convertible maturity it could not fund, management chose a dilutive 2025 debt-for-debt exchange plus large new share issuance to extend maturities to 2030 and avoid bankruptcy, while attempting to restore gross margin and reposition the brand.
action_taken: Cut costs and improved gross margin back to positive in 2024, then in late September 2025 launched a restructuring exchanging over $800 million of convertible notes for new higher-interest bonds and issuing 100+ million new shares, pushing the debt wall from 2027 to 2030.
outcome_evidence: Beyond Meat retained a multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue base but bled cash (net losses of $338.1M in 2023 and $160.3M in 2024, deeply negative Q4 2023 gross margin) and, with ~$1.2B debt against ~$131M cash, had to restructure its convertible notes in 2025 to avoid an otherwise likely bankruptcy, confirming a high-revenue-but-cash/margin crisis.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned 403; figures confirmed verbatim in WebSearch snippets attributed to Beyond Meat's FY2023/FY2024 10-Ks and earnings releases plus named journalism (TheStreet, Yahoo Finance, AgFunderNews): revenues $464.7M (2021) / $343.4M (2023) / $326.5M (2024), net losses $338.1M (2023) / $160.3M (2024), Q4 2023 gross loss $83.9M / -113.8%, 2024 gross profit $41.7M, ~$131.1M cash and ~$1.2B debt at 9/27/2025, >$800M notes exchanged. The 2025 restructuring details are recent and partly journalism-sourced; bankruptcy was averted, not incurred.
directly_stated: Net revenues fell from $464.7 million in 2021 to $343.4 million in 2023 and $326.5 million in 2024
Net loss was $338.1 million in 2023 and $160.3 million in 2024
Q4 2023 gross loss was $83.9 million, a gross margin of -113.8%
2024 gross profit returned to a positive $41.7 million
As of September 27, 2025 the company held about $131.1 million in cash against approximately $1.2 billion of debt
In late September 2025 Beyond Meat moved to exchange over $800 million of convertible notes for new higher-interest bonds plus large share issuance
inferred: The core diagnosis is margin erosion plus debt-driven cash strain on a shrinking-but-still-material revenue base, not a single-shock event
Without the 2025 convertible-note restructuring the looming 2027 maturity would likely have forced bankruptcy
why_useful_for_opsiq: High-revenue-but-cash/margin-crisis (outcome 7) case where a still-material revenue base coexists with negative/thin gross margins, persistent losses, and an unmanageable debt maturity. Tests whether the engine identifies margin_erosion plus debt strain (not demand alone) as the diagnosis on a company that still books hundreds of millions in revenue, and credits margin repair plus debt restructuring as the phase-correct actions.
